parts.solution_md:
(i) *Using the law: *$a^{m}\diva^{n}=a^{m-n}$* rewrite the left hand side*

$x^{10-k}=x^{3}$

> *As both sides have the same base, the powers must be equal*

$10-k=3$

> *Solve to find *$k$

$\begin{gathered} 10 = 3 + k \\ 7 = k \end{gathered}$

$k=7$ **[1]**

(ii) *Using the law: *$a^{m}\timesa^{n}=a^{m+n}$* rewrite the left hand side*

$y^{10+n}=1$

> *Any value to the power of zero is equal to 1*

$y^{10+n}=y^{0}$

> *So *$10+n$* must be equal to zero*

$10+n=0$

> *Solve to find *$n$

$n=-10$ **[1]**

(i) *Using the law of indices we can rewrite the left hand side of the equation.*

> $2^{8}\times2^{m}=2^{8+m}$* *

* *$2^{8+m}=2^{6}$

> *Comparing both sides, the bases are the same, and so we can say that *

> * *$8+m=6$* *

> *Subtract *$8$* from both sides.*

$m=6-8$

$m=-2$* ***[1]**

(ii) *Using the law of indices we can rewrite the left hand side of the equation. *

> $5^{n}\div5^{4}=5^{n-4}$* *

* *$5^{n-4}=5^{6}$

> *Comparing both sides, the bases are the same, and so we can say that *

> * *$n-4=6$* *

> *Add *$4$* to both sides.*

$n=6+4$

$n=10$* ***[1]**
